import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 372

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/372](https://www.erdosproblems.com/372)

Conjectured by Erdős and Pomerance. Proved by Balog, who showed the stronger quantitative result
that this holds for $\gg \sqrt{x}$ many $n\leq x$, for all large $x$.
-/

namespace Erdos372

/--
Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. There are infinitely many $n$ such that
$P(n)>P(n+1)>P(n+2)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_372 :
    {n : ℕ | Nat.maxPrimeFac n > Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 1) ∧
      Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 1) > Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos372

reformulations.difference: The Lean set ranges over all natural numbers, without explicitly requiring n > 1 to avoid the exceptional values of the largest-prime-factor function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 1, Nat.maxPrimeFac is the greatest prime divisor. Its values at 0, 1, and 2 are respectively 0, 1, and 2, so the first strict inequality fails for both n = 0 and n = 1. Thus every member already satisfies n > 1. The scratch file proves equality with the explicitly restricted set and the corresponding infinitude equivalence, without using erdos_372.
